chunks: 5363 - Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿImrān al-Ashʿarī narrated from Muḥammad ibn Nājiyah, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Any wet nurse of a people who kills their infant while she is asleep, by rolling over onto him and thereby killing him, then only the blood money is upon her from her own wealth if she had only taken up wet nursing in pursuit of honor and pride. But if she had only become a wet nurse because of poverty, then the blood money is upon her ʿāqilah.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: blood money paid as legal compensation for wrongful death
key_terms.عَاقِلَتِهَا: her paternal kin group legally responsible for certain compensation payments
key_terms.مِنْ مَالِهَا خَاصَّةً: from her own personal wealth exclusively

ai.seo_question: Who pays the blood money if a wet nurse accidentally kills a child in her sleep?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a wet nurse who accidentally causes the death of a child by rolling onto the child in her sleep. It distinguishes between whether she undertook wet nursing out of pride and status or out of poverty, assigning the diyah either to her personal wealth or to her ʿaqilah accordingly.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5363 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran Al-Ash'ari narrated from Muhammad ibn Najiyah, who narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali, who narrated from Abd Al-Rahman ibn Salim, who narrated from his father, who narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"Any wet nurse of a people who accidentally kills their child while sleeping - by rolling over and causing the child's death - the blood money is to be paid from her personal wealth if she took on nursing for the sake of pride and honor.
However, if she undertook nursing due to poverty, then the blood money is upon her family ('Aqilah)."
